advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure an in-unit RemovedInputError on the background boot-sweep thread still fails the server closed (e.g. signal main() to exit non-zero or mark /health not-ready) rather than being downgraded to an ERROR log while the server keeps serving.
evidence: Primary/fatal failure: a load-bearing removed input surfaced from inside an ensure unit (RemovedInputError). src/rebar/_deprecations.py:77 'class RemovedInputError(BaseException):' — a BaseException, so it is NOT caught by run_ensures' Exception handlers (src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:167 'except Exception as exc' and :177 'except Exception as exc') and propagates out of run_ensures.

Old surfaced disposition (before this diff): run_startup_store_sweep ran synchronously inside main() (removed mcp_server.py call 'run_startup_store_sweep()'); its handler re-raised RemovedInputError ('except RemovedInputError: raise') so it propagated out of main() and aborted startup fail-closed — a fatal, orchestrator-visible condition.

New surfaced disposition (after this diff): src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:323-330 '_sweep_store' runs on a daemon thread; 'if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread(): raise' is False off the main thread, so the branch falls through to logging.getLogger("rebar").error(...) and the server continues serving — the fatal abort is downgraded to a log line.

Caller/classifier whose behavior changes: the container restart orchestrator / supervisor. Pre-change it saw a non-zero startup exit (crash loop, operator-recoverable); post-change the process serves and /health returns 200 — src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:373-375 '/health stays 200 even with a degraded store' and store_status (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:256-278) only checks os.path.isdir and never runs ensures, so the removed-input fault is invisible to the probe.
src/rebar/mcp_server.py:569 'start_startup_store_sweep(getattr(server, _GAUGE_ATTR, None))' is the only caller and does not branch on the result; nothing re-surfaces the swallowed fatal disposition.
advisory.finding: A RemovedInputError raised from inside an ensure unit, which previously aborted MCP startup (fail-closed, main-thread propagation), is downgraded to an ERROR log on the background sweep thread while the server keeps serving, masking a fatal load-bearing-input removal from the restart orchestrator.
scenarios: A still-set but removed load-bearing input is referenced only from within an ensure unit (not from config composition or env tombstone resolution), so it is not caught by the synchronous _resolve_startup_tracker path and only trips once run_ensures executes the unit on the daemon thread.

A crash-restarted container boots, the sweep thread hits the removed input, logs ERROR, and the orchestrator's /health check passes — the container serves against a store whose ensure sweep fail-closed, with no restart or escalation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the daemon-thread RemovedInputError branch record a fatal-startup flag that run_mcp / the SIGTERM path checks (or trip a readiness fault surfaced by store_status) so the orchestrator still sees a fail-closed container, instead of only logging ERROR and continuing to serve.

evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:331-332: `except Exception:` then `logging.getLogger("rebar").debug("startup ensure-sweep skipped", exc_info=True)`

The sweep now runs on a detached daemon thread (`spawn_context_daemon(lambda: _sweep_store(tracker), name="rebar-mcp-boot-sweep")`, line 312), so its only disposition is this log; no caller inspects a return value or completion status.

ABSENCE: nothing records that the sweep actually ran run_ensures to completion vs. skipped on lock contention vs. raised — a crashed background sweep and a converged one both produce no operator-visible output. Litmus: in the world 'the sweep raised inside run_ensures', the system looks identical to 'the sweep converged cleanly'.
dropped.finding: A background boot-sweep failure is swallowed at DEBUG level, so after the sweep moved onto a detached daemon thread there is no observable signal distinguishing 'swept and converged' from 'sweep crashed/aborted'. The sweep's only success/failure disposition is a DEBUG log that is suppressed under the default stderr handler.
scenarios: A boot sweep that aborts on an unexpected store error logs only at DEBUG; operators running default logging see a healthy /health and assume convergence.
dropped.suggested_fix: In _sweep_store's generic `except Exception`, log at WARNING with the sweep name/tracker so a background-thread failure is surfaced instead of swallowed at DEBUG.
